turns.prompt_text: can you show me the differences in paper sizes from letter legal A4 85 B5 B6
turns.response_html:
Understanding the physical dimensions of paper is much easier when you can see how they stack up against each other. Generally, these sizes fall into two categories: the North American standards (Letter/Legal) and the ISO International standards (A-series and B-series).

Quick Comparison Table Table

Here is how these sizes break down by their exact dimensions:

Paper SizeDimensions (Inches)Dimensions (mm)Primary Use
Letter8.5 x 11 in216 x 279 mmStandard US Office use
Legal8.5 x 14 in216 x 356 mmContracts and legal documents
A48.27 x 11.69 in210 x 297 mmStandard International use
B56.9 x 9.8 in176 x 250 mmNotebooks and textbooks
B64.9 x 6.9 in125 x 176 mmFlyers and small pocket books

The Key Differences

1. Letter vs. A4

These two are often confused because they are the "standard" in their respective regions.

  • Letter is wider by about 6mm.
  • A4 is taller by about 18mm. If you try to print an A4 document on Letter paper, the bottom usually gets cut off.

2. Letter vs. Legal

Both share the same width (8.5 inches), but Legal is 3 inches longer. It was originally designed so that lawyers could write lengthy notes in the margins of contracts.

3. The B-Series (B5 & B6)

The B-series is the "middle ground" of the international system.

  • B5 is roughly 70% the size of an A4 sheet. It’s a very popular size for high-quality journals and composition books because it’s easier to carry than a full A4 but larger than a standard 5x7 photo.
  • B6 is essentially half the size of B5. It is a common size for paperback books and personal planners.

A Note on "85"

If you saw "85" on a printer setting or a paper pack, it is almost certainly a typo or a shorthand for B5. There is no standard "85" size, though some niche cardstock manufacturers use custom numbering.
